props.title: Little Buddha

sections.content: Little Buddha (1993) marks a fascinating intersection of Eastern spirituality and Western filmmaking by acclaimed director Bernardo Bertolucci. The film weaves together two parallel narratives: the historical story of Prince Siddhartha's transformation into the Buddha, and a contemporary tale of Tibetan monks searching for a reincarnated lama in Seattle. Keanu Reeves' casting as Siddhartha sparked controversy but achieves an otherworldly quality that serves the mythological aspects. Like Bertolucci's earlier The Last Emperor (1987), the film employs rich cinematography and careful attention to period detail while exploring cultural bridges between East and West.

sections.content: The 1990s saw a surge of Western films exploring Buddhism and Tibetan culture, partly influenced by China's occupation of Tibet and growing celebrity advocacy. Kundun (1997) takes a more historically grounded approach than Little Buddha, while Seven Years in Tibet (1997) uses a Western protagonist as an entry point. These films share gorgeous Himalayan landscapes and attempts to translate Buddhist concepts for Western audiences, though Little Buddha remains unique in its parallel ancient/modern structure. SUBHEAD: Buddhist Themes in Contemporary Cinema

Beyond explicit Buddhist subjects, films like The Matrix (1999) and Groundhog Day (1993) incorporate Buddhist concepts like enlightenment, rebirth, and liberation from illusion. Lost Horizon (1937) established many tropes about Westerners encountering Tibetan wisdom that later films both drew from and subverted. Modern works like Doctor Strange (2016) continue mining Eastern spirituality, though often superficially. Little Buddha stands out for its sincere attempt to present Buddhist teachings without exoticizing them.
